findings.title: Refused legacy termination loses its cleanup owner
findings.reproduction: Publish a real native child's PID into the legacy state machine. Claim a published start failure. Inject refusal into both termination operations without changing the finalizer's state transitions. Observe true cleanup receipt and Finished=true with no registry entry while a zero-time wait on an independently retained process handle proves the child alive. The isolated repro.patch safely supervises and cleans up its own child.
findings.root_cause: Legacy failure/termination removes registry ownership before physical teardown. _SR_LegacyBeginFinalize consumes the claim before fallible cleanup; _SR_LegacyTerminateClaim logs refusal but returns true and leaves no retry owner. The native creator already closed its process capability and retained only a PID.
findings.silent_failure: Errors may be logged, but the caller receives successful cleanup and cannot retry the consumed terminal claim. Existing state-machine tests prove callback retirement without checking process exit or retained cleanup debt.
findings.regression_test: Exercise refusal/retry for published and private start failure, explicit and reentrant cancellation, stale snapshots and identifier reuse. Require exact native ownership until observed exit and successful cleanup, retained captures, zero stale callbacks and healthy native controls; preserve legacy descendant semantics.

findings.title: Legacy native child failure is reported as success
findings.reproduction: Through the unchanged public ShellRunner_Spawn path, launch the attached native AHK child that writes legacy-exit-37 and exits with code 37. Observe the intended marker in OnDone but exit code zero. The exit_code_repro.patch adds only test fixtures and registration; it changes no production operation.
findings.root_cause: _SR_LegacyCreateDirect closes the original process handle immediately after resuming the child. _SR_Poll waits for ProcessExist(Pid) to become false, then _SR_GetExitCode attempts to reopen the already collected process and silently returns zero when it cannot.
findings.silent_failure: The completion callback receives a success-shaped zero rather than the child's actual failure, and the unavailable process handle is deliberately mapped to zero. Existing native argv tests can pass with a successful child without testing failure propagation.
findings.regression_test: Require exact nonzero exit codes and output for fast native children through the public launcher, plus zero-exit controls, delayed completion under suspension, duplicate polling and stale identity cases. Read status from the original retained native handle and never fabricate success after a failed query.
